correctness.rationale: The exact sharp frame bounds and unique global optimizer for this normalized window and integer-density rectangular lattice are quoted with explicit source and scope (Faulhuber–Shafkulovska, Eq. 8.1 and Thm. 2.7). The algebraic factorization follows because b(x)/a(x)=cosh(x). The prior optimizer bracket gives eta comparable to log(q). Uniform Taylor expansions of the exact factorization and its exact differentiated factors give F'=tanh(eta/q)/q-4eta \(e^{-\eta}\)+controlled error. Stationarity then implies \(e^{-\eta}\)=1/(4q^2)(1+\(O((\log q)^2/q^2)\)), whence the claimed sharp location. Substitution yields all three coefficients in the minimal condition-number excess and an \(O((\log q)^4/q^4)\) remainder. The finite high-precision checker confirms critical equations and residual trends but is not offered as a proof of the infinite asymptotic. Domain, normalization, and dependencies are explicit.

originality.rationale: The core object and parameter are exactly those of a 2023 sharp-bound/uniqueness paper; this potentially dominating source was inspected rather than disregarded. Its sharp formulas and uniqueness are not claimed as new. Its optimizer theorem confines eta to an O(log q) interval, and its condition-number section does not state the vanishing additive optimizer error or three-term optimized conditioning expansion. Those require the new uniform stationary-point balance. The 2026 totally-positive frame-set theorem provides a broader *qualitative* frame-existence conclusion, not a sharp optimized lattice. Nearby indexed results concern different signals, lattices, or functionals. Unindexed supplements and historical literature remain explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: A quantitatively equivalent expansion could appear in the 1996 original Janssen work, a 2023 supplement, or another incompletely indexed paper; not all older full texts were available/inspected.
The 2023 exact functions logically support further derived asymptotics; the claim distinguishes new asymptotic analysis from any prior entitlement to the exact finite-density bound formulas.

value.rationale: The exact best-condition-number problem for rectangular exponential Gabor frames is structurally motivated by stable high-density time-frequency sampling. The result sharpens a previously broad logarithmic-width localization to an additive \(O((\log q)^2/q^2)\) window, and computes the full \(q^{-2}\) optimized spectral excess including log-squared, log and constant coefficients, rather than merely observing eventual tightness. The balance of a frequency-fiber \(x^2/2\) term and an exponentially decaying boundary term identifies the natural high-density design scale. Neither an arbitrary slice nor a tiny gain on a predetermined numerical benchmark.
